observations: Photo 0 shows a disassembled car engine (V-type, turbocharged) sitting on a shop floor.
A black plastic intake cover reads 'Turbo' with a partial logo, but no engine code, VIN, or brand plate is legible.

claims.claim: We also deal on all kinds of car spare parts such as Volkswagen, Audi, Porsche and Bentley
claims.evidence: This is a general business claim about inventory range, not shown or provable from the single engine photo.

risks.risk: Exact make/model/engine code unknown, which drives most of the price difference between VW, Audi, Porsche, and Bentley parts
risks.proof: Close-up photo of the engine code plate/sticker (usually on block or cam cover) or a VIN tag from the donor car
risks.if_unproven: priced at the lowest-value generic 'used turbo engine, unidentified VAG-type' tier

risks.risk: Running condition unknown (no start-up, compression, or oil state evidence)
risks.proof: Video of engine cranking/running or a compression test reading

risks.risk: Completeness unclear (turbo unit, sensors, ECU, wiring harness may or may not be included)
risks.proof: Full 360-degree photos including front, rear, and underside of the engine

risks.risk: Mileage/history and reason for removal unknown (accident, flood, high mileage)
risks.proof: Donor vehicle documents or odometer photo

proof_requests: Close-up of engine code plate or any sticker with model/part number
Video of the engine running or being cranked
Full set of photos from all sides including the turbo unit and wiring harness
Any documentation (import papers, donor car details) showing origin and mileage
response.reason: The engine's brand and model cannot be read from the photo, and price ranges for VW vs Porsche vs Bentley parts are too wide to assign even a worst-case figure without that identification.
